adults.shape: elongated with long snouts and elbowed antennae
adults.metallic_sheen: subtle when newly emerged, dulls with age
adults.comparison: smaller and less abruptly curved snouts than M. janthiniformis

life_cycle.overwintering_stage: adult in previous year's toadflax stems
life_cycle.spring_emergence: early spring, timing varies by site-specific factors
life_cycle.adult_feeding: new shoot tips and leaves, produces shot hole injury pattern

egg_laying.method: females chew holes in stems, lay eggs singly, cover with chewed plant tissue

life_cycle.larval_feeding: 3 instars, mine lower stems in tunnels
life_cycle.adult_emergence: late summer, overwinter inside pupal chambers

adult: weakens plants, suppresses flowering and seed production
stunts shoots, shoot tips turn brown and shrivel
larval: causes desiccation and death of plant tissue
likely depletes root nutrient reserves, impacting plant persistence
damage.long_term_impact: Repeated yearly attack reduces toadflax plant density

management_notes: Biocontrol agent used against invasive toadflax in North America
Monitoring adult emergence in spring can guide management strategies
Supports long-term reduction of toadflax populations
references: Sing, S.E., De Clerck-Floate, R.A., Randall, C.B., Toševski, I. 2022. Toadflax Biocontrol Agents: History and Ecology in North America. In: Biological Control of Weeds in North America. NAISMA-BCW-2022-29-TOADFLAXES-A.
